sections.h2: Who handles what in South Fulton
sections.html:
South Fulton is a young city with an unusual setup. It took over zoning, police, fire and code enforcement when it took effect on May 1, 2017, yet property valuation and tax billing still run through Fulton County. That split decides which office you call about each piece of a sale.

The 2020 census counted 107,436 residents, which made South Fulton the state's eighth-largest city. It was carved from southwest Fulton County and takes in many older communities that kept their names, such as Red Oak, Cooks Crossing, Fife, Ben Hill, Sandtown, Cliftondale, Cedar Grove, Enon and Welcome All. Buyers and agents still describe houses by those names. Confirm the tax district and zoning for your exact address before you sign anything.

The Old National Highway corridor is the city's main commercial street, with a large revitalization planned along it, so a seller nearby may hear questions about construction and future uses. Fulton County Schools serves the entire city, and the city runs no school district. Attendance boundaries can change by street, so point buyers to the school system's own address lookup instead of promising a school assignment in the listing.

Water, trash pickup, elections and public health are handled by Fulton County or private companies, not the city. If you hand a buyer a list of the house's services, name the county or company so the right office gets the call at closing.

sections.h2: Permits for repairs before a sale
sections.html:
The city's Development Services division, part of Community Development and Regulatory Affairs, handles permits, and applications are filed through the SagesGov portal. Permit staff can be reached at 470-809-7200, extension 1, between 8:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. The division processes these residential items:

  • New construction and demolitions
  • Alterations, additions and renovations
  • Sheds and fences
  • Retaining walls
  • Mechanical, electrical and plumbing trade permits

Inspections are scheduled in the same portal, and a request made before 4 p.m. can be conducted the next business day. State minimum construction codes now include the 2024 International Residential Code with Georgia amendments, so contractors should be working to the newer editions. If you plan only light repairs, call the permitting line before starting and ask whether the work needs a permit. Skipping that step can cause trouble when a buyer's inspector or the city's code staff notices.

sections.h2: Can I sell a South Fulton house that I rented short term?
sections.html:
Yes, but the permit status should be clean before you list. In 2025 the city dropped its Special Use Permit requirement for short-term rentals and replaced it with a standard permit application. The city defines a short-term rental as lodging for no more than 30 consecutive days, and rentals are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

The application can be emailed or dropped off at City Hall. A non-refundable $200 application fee is invoiced after the city receives and approves the application at intake. Running a rental without a valid permit may bring fines, penalties or suspension, and repeated violations can lead to denial of later applications. The city also posts a running list of permit applications marked approved, denied or pending, and it accepts public comment on pending ones.

Short-term rental permit topicRule
Permit typeStandard STR permit; Special Use Permit no longer required as of 2025
DefinitionLodging for a period not exceeding 30 consecutive days
Where allowedResidential zoning districts only
Application fee$200, non-refundable, invoiced after intake approval
Without a permitFines, penalties or suspension of rental activity

If a permit is pending or was denied, tell a buyer up front. Ask the city's community development staff whether a permit carries over to a new owner before you promise a buyer anything about future rental use.

sections.h2: South Fulton property taxes and appeals
sections.html:
The City of South Fulton states that its property taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, while the Board of Assessors sets value, accepts homestead applications and handles appeals. Recent notices of assessment show estimated tax savings rather than an estimated tax bill, following a change in state law.

An appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date, online, by mail or in person, and an appeal covers value only. When you file, choose a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration or a hearing officer. Fees may apply on some routes. A temporary bill can arrive while the appeal is open, and it still has to be paid.

Homestead applications filed after the April 1 deadline can be accepted during the appeal window for owners who held the home on January 1. The South Fulton Service Center for both the assessors and the tax commissioner is at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road. The assessors' phone line is 404-612-6440 and the tax commissioner's is 404-613-6100.

sections.h2: What a South Fulton seller should expect at closing
sections.html:
Plan on a deed recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court of Fulton County and a transfer tax payment tied to that recording. Questions about taxability and exemptions go to the clerk of the county where the property sits. Your closing attorney will also look for unpaid taxes and code liens, since both can delay a deed.

Owners who want a sure thing often line up an agent listing, an as-is investor sale and a direct cash sale side by side. Repairs, timing and the cash you need left over after liens and taxes will point to the winner.

Get a draft settlement statement a few days ahead of closing and read the payoff, tax lines and lien releases against your own records. Questions are easier to settle early. Even when a cash buyer skips loan approval, the deed, the transfer tax and the lien search still take place, and your attorney handles each one. Allow a little extra time if an open permit or a short-term rental record needs sorting out first.

sections.h2: Steps before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Call the permitting line and ask about any past work that needed a permit or still has one open.
  2. Find out if the house was ever rented short term and where that permit stands.
  3. Ask the Fulton County offices for the current tax bill and any open balance.
  4. Collect an agent's opinion of value and a written cash offer, and compare the net after liens and taxes.
  5. Hand the closing attorney your deed and let the attorney search for liens early.

An investor paying cash can take on open permit items or a half-finished repair. A lender may refuse, which is why how you handle these loose ends decides which offers stay on the table, and a clear record also gives you a stronger hand in any price talk.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a South Fulton house?
faqs.a: Fulton County does. The city says its taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my South Fulton assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the notice of assessment. After that deadline, your right to appeal that year's value is lost.

faqs.q: Do I need a Special Use Permit to run a short-term rental in South Fulton?
faqs.a: No. Since 2025 the city uses a standard STR permit with a $200 non-refundable application fee, and rentals are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

faqs.q: Can I fix up my house without a permit before selling?
faqs.a: Only for work the city does not regulate. Alterations, additions, renovations, sheds, fences and trade work such as electrical and plumbing go through the permitting division.

faqs.q: Which county office handles the deed when I sell?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court of Fulton County records the deed after the transfer tax is paid. Exemption questions go to that clerk.
